title: Component Interaction Diagram - Real-Time Data Flow
context: 9router application real-time infrastructure: chatCore → executors → translators → SSE out, model routing, combo caps, TTS flow

chatCore.internal pipeline: parseModel → RTK compress → translateRequest → post-translate savers → getExecutor → executor.execute → translateResponse → SSE out
chatCore.key responsibility: Format detection, translation orchestration, streaming pipe management, error handling for aborts and stalls

executors.specialization: One executor per provider type (codex, gemini-cli, cursor, bedrock, etc.); DefaultExecutor falls back to OpenAI-compatible API when no specialized executor exists
executors.key responsibility: Execute upstream API call, stream raw response chunks back through the pipeline

translator.pipeline: request translation: source→openai→target (or direct route if registered); response translation: target→openai→source (or direct route)
translator.direct routes: Registered translator pairs avoid double-hop through OpenAI: e.g., claude↔kiro, openai-responses↔codex, gemini↔openai
translator.key responsibility: Convert between client format (OpenAI chat completions/Responses) and provider-native format; handle tool_calls, thinking, reasoning, role renaming

model routing.flow: parseModel → resolveProviderAlias → getModelInfo → getProviderCredentials → enforceKeyAccess → handleChatCore → (combo: handleComboChat/handleFusionChat) → handleSingleModelChat → chatCore
model routing.combo resolution: getComboModels → reorderByCapabilities (by hard/soft caps) → getRotatedModels (fallback/round-robin/fusion) → auto-switch float capable models to front → handleComboChat iterates rotated list with fallback on error/zero-content
model routing.fusion: handleFusionChat fans prompt to all panel models in parallel, collects with quorum-grace, judge model synthesizes final answer
model routing.key responsibility: Resolve which provider/model handles each request, handle fallbacks, rotation, and fusion

outputs: required capabilities Set (vision, pdf, audioInput, videoInput, search, tools, reasoning)
reordered model list by capability fit
combo caps resolution.hard capabilities: vision, pdf, audioInput, videoInput - missing one drops request data
combo caps resolution.soft capabilities: search, tools, reasoning - degrade feature but don't drop
combo caps resolution.pattern matching: PATTERN_CAPABILITIES array of glob patterns (ordered specific→generic) → MODEL_CAPABILITIES exact overrides → PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES provider overrides → DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES safe floor
combo caps resolution.aggregateComboCapabilities: Merge capabilities across all models in a combo, respecting provider-specific and exact-id overrides
combo caps resolution.key responsibility: Determine what modalities a request needs, reorder combo models to satisfy capabilities first, aggregate capability state across combo members

SSE out.reliability: pipeWithDisconnect(providerResponse, transformStream, streamController, onAbortTerminal, stallTimeoutMs) - handles client disconnect mid-stream, terminal bytes on abort, stall timeout detection
SSE out.terminal bytes: buildAbortedResponsesTerminalBytes (for Responses passthrough) or buildStreamErrorBytes (for other formats) - client sees real error instead of silent truncation
SSE out.key responsibility: Stream provider SSE through format translators to client; handle disconnects, stalls, and error terminal bytes

files: TBD - not in current codebase but defined in ADR
inputs: cursor position, selection, viewport state per user per room
presence.design: TTL=60s on presence hashes; heartbeat refreshes TTL; silence = gone; coalesced to ≤10 updates/sec; never writes to document log
presence.key responsibility: Who's here + where their cursor is; ephemeral, lossy by design; distinct channel from durable document ops

dataFlowDiagram.description: Client request → chat handler (auth + combo routing) → open-sse handleChatCore → parseModel/resolve credentials → RTK compress → translator translateRequest → post-translate savers (RTK headroom/caveman) → getExecutor → executor.execute (upstream API) → streaming pipe → translator translateResponse → SSE out
sequence: 4. RTK: compress tool_result in-place (fail-open, never throw)
6. post-translate savers: headroom compress proxy, caveman system prompt inject
8. Provider SSE chunks → translateResponse: provider→client format
9. pipeWithDisconnect → SSE response with CORS headers
10. saveRequestDetail → usage DB; onStreamComplete → usage tracking
dataFlowDiagram.responseFlow: Provider SSE chunks → translateResponse (target→openai→source) → client-format JSON → SSE out with proper headers
dataFlowDiagram.modelRoutingFlow: client model string → parseModel → (if alias → resolveModelAliasFromMap) → getModelInfo (from DB/cache) → getProviderCredentials → enforceKeyAccess → if combo → handleComboChat (auto-switch + rotate + fallback) → handleSingleModelChat → chatCore → executor → upstream → translateResponse → SSE
dataFlowDiagram.comboCapsFlow: request body → detectRequiredCapabilities (scan current user turn for vision/audio/pdf) → reorderByCapabilities (tier: all-hard=0, all-hard-only=1, rest=2) → getRotatedModels (fallback/round-robin) → auto-switch float capable models → handleComboChat iterates with zero-content fallback

keyInsights: The open-sse pipeline is modular: chatCore → translator → executor → translator → SSE, with RTK and post-translate savers as cross-cutting concerns
Direct translator routes (e.g., claude↔kiro) skip the lossy OpenAI double-hop
Executor specialization: most providers use DefaultExecutor (OpenAI-compatible); specialized executors handle non-standard upstream APIs (cursor, kiro, commandcode, etc.)
Model routing does credential rotation + combo fallback + capability-aware reordering before dispatching to chatCore
Combo fusion is parallel panel + judge synthesis - highest quality but most expensive (N+1 calls)
SRE patterns (backpressure, stall timeout, abort terminal bytes) are baked into the streaming pipe, not bolted on
Presence (if added) must be separate from durable document ops - TTL-scoped, lossy by design
